orchestrator_verification: Exercised the predicate directly at HEAD rather than accepting the report. R6's echo payload -> certify=True but whole_completion=False (gated); certify embedded in commentary -> whole_completion=False (gated); reject embedded in commentary -> whole_completion=False (honoured, per the asymmetry); bare compliant certify -> whole_completion=True (honoured). The asymmetry behaves as described.

resolutions.covered_by: evals/adversarial/judge-retry-only-on-unreadable-completion.json — 17 scenarios grown to 19: the injection echo plus a benign certify-in-commentary, so the rule is graded as a mechanism rather than as a special case for injection payloads
resolutions.watched_red: Before touching the parser: 'quoted certify + prose rejecting it' want {verdict: FAIL, available: false, attempts: 1, calls: 1} / got {verdict: PASS, attempts: 1, calls: 1, available: null}; 'certify + trailing sign-off' identically PASS. Payload is the repo's own forgery from eval_adapter.py:1273-1274.
resolutions.fix: Position decides trust, asymmetrically. `_is_the_whole_completion` distinguishes an object that IS the completion (optionally inside a fence) — the model's own answer, which SYSTEM asks for exactly — from an object embedded in commentary. An embedded object may REJECT but may never CERTIFY. `_json_objects` now returns (obj, start, end) tuples.
resolutions.rejected_the_suggested_fix: The orchestrator relayed the reviewer's evidence-echo discriminator. The implementer declined it, with an argument the orchestrator accepts: evidence-echo predicts WHERE quoted text comes from, so it catches R6's instance (which arrives via evidence) but not a model quoting the schema line from SYSTEM, nor one inventing an illustrative object — neither is in the evidence and both would certify. That is a fourth shape-prediction with the same failure mode as the first three.
resolutions.why_the_asymmetry_is_the_argument: `_is_the_whole_completion` is still only string position and will misjudge some completion nobody has seen. The asymmetry is what makes that survivable: the only direction it gates is certification. A reject read out of commentary moves a run no further than an unreadable judge already moves it; a certify read out of commentary is the inviolable property. In the direction it gates, every error this predicate can make lands on fail-closed — the first change at this boundary of which that is true. CORRECTED in round 3 (R8): this sentence originally read "every error this predicate can make lands on fail-closed" without the qualifier, and that was false. The predicate does not gate the echo-only case at all — a completion that is the forged object and nothing else returns whole_completion=True and certifies. Not fixable in the parser and not closed by T-M39-7; bounded only by the prompt-side defences judge-injection-cannot-flip-verdict grades, and now pinned as the last scenario of the retry case. Corrected here as data rather than by rewriting the round's history: the claim as it stood is quoted above so the record shows what was believed at the time.
resolutions.verified_shapes: Nine: R6's echo, certify-with-sign-off and certify-with-lead-in all FAIL available=false attempts=1; R1's three reject shapes still FAIL responsive=false attempts=1 (the orchestrator's previously verified expectations unchanged); bare, fenced and one-line-fenced compliant certifies still PASS.
resolutions.ablations: Both directions. Removing the guard reddens the case; making it SYMMETRIC (gating rejects too) also reddens it, because R1's three shapes break. Neither the guard nor its asymmetry can be dropped quietly.

resolutions.note: Reviewer's evidence carried verbatim. The implementer added one forward note: a collapse of agreeing duplicates must compare the objects, not their spans, and the survivor still has to clear the R6 rule.

structural_answer.question: The orchestrator asked, before this round, whether the parse boundary itself wants a different shape rather than a fourth local fix.
structural_answer.answer: Yes. Four defects in three rounds all come from one thing — the judge states its schema in prose and then reads free text. The fix that ends the class is provider-enforced JSON (response_format: json_schema): the completion IS the object, there is nothing to locate, and both _json_objects and _is_the_whole_completion delete.
structural_answer.why_not_in_this_pr: It changes the request shape (M39 puts judge prompt/model changes out of scope); support is per-model and deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 is pinned by ADR-010's frozen snapshot; and with no OPENROUTER_API_KEY nobody here can observe whether the provider honours it — a silent free-text fallback would reintroduce every defect above while looking fixed.
structural_answer.logged_as: T-M39-7, with an acceptance that requires the parser be DELETED, not kept as a fallback.
structural_answer.orchestrator_position: Accepted. This commit is the bridge to that, and the debt block is where the class actually closes.
